item.title: Account Director (Litigation Specialist)
item.description: Join the PubAffairs Network Established in January 2002, PubAffairs is the premier network and leading resource for the public affairs, government relations, policy and communications industry. The PubAffairs network numbers over 4,000 members and is free to join. PubAffairs operates a general e-Newsletter, as well as a number of other specific group e-Newsletters which are also available to join by completing our registration form. The PubAffairs e-Newsletters are used to keep members informed about upcoming PubAffairs events and networking opportunities, job vacancies, public affairs news, training courses, stakeholder events, publications, discount offers and other pieces of useful information related to the public affairs and communications industry. Join the Network

item.title: Account Director (Health | Life Sciences | Public Affairs)
item.description: PLMR Healthcomms a leading UK healthcare public affairs and communications consultancy. We help organisations get health innovation moving. Working across pharmaceuticals, medical technology, diagnostics, digital health and the wider NHS, we help clients navigate complex policy and NHS structures to turn innovation into real-world impact. As the NHS continues to evolve, organisations need advisers who understand how decisions are made across government, Parliament and the NHS. Our team combines expertise in health policy, public affairs, strategic communications and stakeholder engagement to help clients shape policy, build trust and accelerate adoption. As part of the wider PLMR Group, we bring together specialists in communications, digital, political intelligence and AI-enabled insight to deliver integrated campaigns that influence policy, change perceptions and create measurable impact. We judge our success by the difference we make for our clients - whether that's influencing policy, strengthening partnerships, changing conversations or helping innovative products and services reach patients more quickly. Key Responsibilities and Duties We're looking for an experienced and ambitious Account Director to help lead the next stage of PLMR Healthcomms' growth. This is an opportunity to work at the heart of some of the most important challenges facing healthcare today. You will be supporting organisations to navigate NHS reform, shape policy, build stakeholder confidence and ultimately improve patient access to medicines, technologies and services. You will act as a trusted adviser to clients across pharmaceuticals, medical technology, diagnostics and digital health, helping them move from ambition to action. Alongside leading strategic client programmes, you will play an important role in developing our growing healthcare practice, supporting new business, mentoring colleagues and helping strengthen PLMR Healthcomms' reputation as the consultancy that gets health innovation moving. The ideal candidate will bring: A passion for improving healthcare through policy, communications and stakeholder engagement. Significant experience advising pharmaceutical, life sciences or health technology organisations, ideally with agency experience. An excellent understanding of the NHS, Government, Parliament and the wider healthcare policy landscape. Confidence advising senior clients through complex policy, political and reputational challenges. A commercial mindset and enthusiasm for helping grow both clients and the wider business. A collaborative approach and a desire to develop colleagues while contributing to a supportive, ambitious team. Key Skills and Competencies Significant experience in healthcare public affairs, integrated communications or healthcare consultancy. A strong understanding of the political and NHS landscape and how healthcare decisions are made. Experience advising pharmaceutical, medtech or life sciences organisations. A track record of leading strategic client relationships and delivering measurable outcomes. Excellent commercial awareness and experience contributing to business growth. Outstanding communication, leadership and mentoring skills. Curiosity, ambition and a desire to help shape the future of healthcare. To Apply Please click the Apply button below to find out more about this role. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Saturday 31st October 2026

item.title: Head of Advocacy and Engagement
item.description: FGF is a progressive, non-partisan think tank focused on transforming the state with the ultimate goal of renewing the nation. We build strong networks and convene experts from across the public, private and social sectors to develop and test new and innovative ways in which government could be more effective at every level, and we make politically credible recommendations for reforms that can be delivered nationally and locally. With our three-year strategy, a growing team, and expanding networks in central, local and regional government, civil society and business, this is an exciting time to join FGF. This new role will be pivotal to our growing business. A key member of FGF’s senior management team, you will be responsible for overseeing our business development activities and for building relationships and advocating for FGF’s work with key stakeholders in government, parliament, the civil service, the commercial sector, academics and civil society. You will need to be an excellent communicator, with a track record of writing successful funding bids and significant senior-level experience in central or local government, political party, think tank or not-for-profit organisation. item.title: Executive Liaison to CEO (Maternity Cover)
item.description: The Nature Friendly Farming Network (NFFN) is a farmer-led organisation helping farmers restore the balance between farming and nature. We support farmers by sharing knowledge, resources and case studies that help boost food production, protect wildlife, and build climate resilience. We influence policy to secure fair rewards for farmers who care for nature, and we connect like-minded farmers across the UK. Our network is open to all: farmers, the public and partner organisations. About the Role Help shape the future of nature-friendly farming by supporting the CEO’s political, policy and external engagement. We are looking for an Executive Liaison to CEO to maintain continuity during maternity leave, coordinating a fast-moving programme of work with government, Parliament, funders, partners and senior stakeholders. Working closely with the CEO and Head of Policy, you will connect external engagement with colleagues across NFFN, helping turn senior relationships and policy opportunities into practical progress. You will also support governance coordination and effective working between the CEO, Chair, Board and Senior Leadership Team. Your work will include: Coordinate the CEO’s diary, meetings and forward programme, making effective use of their time. Research and prepare political and stakeholder briefings, correspondence and presentations. Build senior relationships and support the CEO at parliamentary events, conferences and stakeholder meetings. Share intelligence across NFFN and ensure actions, commitments and opportunities are followed through. Support coordination between the CEO, Chair, Board and Senior Leadership Team. You will bring experience in a parliamentary or policy setting, sound political judgement and the ability to turn complex information into clear briefings and practical actions. Strong organisation, excellent communication, discretion and confidence working with senior stakeholders are essential, alongside a commitment to nature-friendly farming. Knowledge of agricultural and environmental policy would be an advantage. This is a 12-month maternity cover post, with an expected start in mid-December 2026 (exact date to be agreed). The contract includes an initial handover before maternity leave and a return handover when the substantive postholder resumes work. Regular travel across the UK is required to support and accompany the CEO at meetings, events and other engagements, most frequently to the CEO’s farm in Cambridgeshire and to London, including Parliament. Some locations may be rural or not easily accessible by public transport. Occasional overnight stays may be required. A driving licence or access to a car is not required. Travel arrangements will depend on what is practical and reasonable for the organisation. Reasonable business travel and accommodation expenses are covered in accordance with NFFN’s expenses policy. Reasonable adjustments will be considered where appropriate. To Apply Please click the Apply button below to find out more about this role and to download the Role Profile. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. We reserve the right to close applications early if we receive a strong field of applications or identify a suitable candidate before the advertised closing date. We therefore encourage candidates to apply as early as possible. Phone screens: During the week of closing (exact dates to be confirmed). Interviews: Week commencing Oct 26, 2026. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 9:00am on Wednesday 21st October 2026

item.title: Public Affairs Consultant
item.description: We are looking to hire a Public Affairs Consultant to join our expanding team. NorthPoint works where politics, regulation, reputation and the media intersect. We help organisations navigate that environment, influence policy and public discourse, and protect their standing when the stakes matter. Our strength lies in understanding how decisions are made, how reputations are formed and how organisations can engage effectively with Government, regulators and the media. We provide senior counsel that helps clients anticipate change, manage risk and act decisively at the moments that matter most. We advise organisations across the public, private and third sectors, from ambitious start-ups and scale-ups to established national and global outfits. We work across a broad range of sectors, with particular expertise in industries where political, regulatory and public scrutiny shapes commercial success. This role encompasses both internal and external responsibilities, requiring an individual who excels in clear, direct communication. It is ideal for someone who: Is a proactive individual with experience in public affairs or government relations. Has strong understanding of Parliament, Government and how policy is shaped and influenced. Has a political and/or public affairs network and is comfortable at networking events. Is happy to get stuck in on new business growth. Can bring a sense of humour and enthusiasm to the table (work doesn't have to be dull). Has agency experience and looking for more autonomy Can cultivate strong relationships with stakeholders across all levels (personality is key, no shrinking violets). To Apply Please click on the Apply button below to email your CV and a short paragraph (no more than a few sentences) about why you'd be a good fit, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. The successful candidate must have permission to work in the UK before the commencement of employment. Interviews will be on a rolling basis and we might appoint a candidate before the closing date. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Monday 26th October 2026

item.title: Stakeholder Engagement and Events Associate
item.description: Join Ofwat’s Communications and Engagement team as a Stakeholder Engagement and Events Associate. We have 1 Fixed Term contract available until the end of December 2027. About Us We’re Ofwat, the Water Services Regulation Authority – a non-ministerial government department responsible for regulating the water sector in England and Wales. As the economic regulator of water and wastewater companies in England and Wales, our role is to enable, incentivise and hold companies to account for providing the very best for customers, communities and the environment. We also oversee the markets in the water sector to ensure they’re working for customers. Following the Independent Water Commission’s Final Report and subsequent White Paper - 'New Vision for Water', the UK government has set out a bold new direction - one that brings together expertise from across the sector to deliver better outcomes for customers and the environment. The Role We're looking for a Stakeholder Engagement and Events Associate to join our team at a crucial time for the water sector. In this role you'll work closely with colleagues across Ofwat, including senior leaders, to support the delivery of external engagement, communications and events with our stakeholders, including consumer organisations, environmental groups, water companies, investors, and more. This will include coordinating the Stakeholder Engagement and Communications team's systems and processes to ensure we're managing our work effectively – including managing our inboxes, speaker requests, activity trackers and databases. You'll also take a hands-on role in delivering engagement and events, attending and supporting engagement events, exhibitions and conferences. You will work in cross-functional project teams on priority communications projects and over time will be given the opportunity to develop in the role and take on stretch responsibilities to design and manage defined engagement and events activities, with support from senior colleagues. Key deliverables In this role you will be expected to: Support the delivery of stakeholder engagement and communications plans and activity across a wide range of projects, including high-profile consultations and announcements. Coordinate and manage key systems and processes for the stakeholder engagement and communications team, including management of inboxes, maintaining stakeholder databases, and ensuring activity trackers are up-to-date and accurate. Coordinate the speaker requests process for Ofwat, ensuring we effectively manage incoming requests for Ofwat staff to speak at external events and conferences; and work with the Events Lead to support the management of our proactive, strategic programme of speaking engagements. Support the preparation and delivery of engagements and events, supporting senior colleagues and stakeholders with their involvement. This may include attendance at exhibitions and conferences and may require occasional travel. Support proactive stakeholder monitoring and insight sharing to support policy development, decision making, and communications and engagement approaches. •roduce high-quality written communications, including correspondence, stakeholder communications, and internal briefings. Work proactively within the wider Communications and Engagement team, supporting additional projects and activities as required. About You Below there are some of the key essential experience, skills & knowledge required for this post: 1. Lead criterion: Excellent organisational skills, with the ability to manage multiple, competing priorities and processes simultaneously while maintaining attention to detail. 2. Experience providing coordination or administrative support within a communications, stakeholder engagement or events context, including managing systems such as inboxes, databased or trackers to a high standard of accuracy. 3. Strong written communication skills, with experience drafting clear and accurate written materials, including correspondence, briefings, or communications for a range of audiences. 4. Experience supporting the planning or delivery of events or engagement, including liaising with speakers, attendees or senior colleagues. Why You Should Join Us: People Centric: Our people are at the heart of Ofwat and everything we do - we ensure all voices are heard and treat each other with respect; you'll be given the autonomy and the support to do your role in the best way. Innovative Work Environment: We embrace agile and new ways of working and have a culture build on trust, flexibility, and collaboration. Development Opportunities: Gain valuable experience and develop your skills in a supportive and dynamic setting. Work-Life Balance: Enjoy the flexibility of working from home combined with the benefits of in person collaboration in our Birmingham offices. Good employer pension contributions 25 days’ annual leave, increasing to 30 with each year of service, plus bank holidays and an extra 2.5 days of privilege leave. Access to exclusive discounts on a variety of goods and services, including retail outlets, theatre tickets, holidays, insurance, and a gym membership. Fees paid for membership of relevant professional bodies. Up to 3 volunteering days per year. Recognition vouchers scheme rewarding your hard work. Generous shared parental leave and pay supporting your family life. * Office Location: London (E14 4HD) or Birmingham (B5 4UA) with hybrid working * To Apply Please click on the Apply button below for more information and to download the Candidate Pack, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Selection timetable Closing date: 23.55 on Sunday 18 October 2026. Sifting: Week commencing 19 October 2026. Interview date(s): Week commencing 2 November 2026. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:55pm on Sunday 18th October 2026

item.title: Public Affairs Officer
item.description: Groundwork UK is looking for a Public Affairs Officer to help put its new three-year public affairs strategy into action. About Us Groundwork UK is the national body of the Groundwork federation, supporting, championing and representing the work of Groundwork Trusts across the country. This includes building national relationships with funders and policymakers, securing resources to support local delivery and acting as a managing agent for programmes and contracts delivered by Groundwork Trusts and other partners. Groundwork takes practical action to create a fair and green future in which people, places, and nature thrive. We support local communities and businesses to build capacity and resilience as this is vital if we are to tackle hardship, achieve a just transition to net-zero and help nature recover in a way that reduces inequality and leads to better work and healthier, happier lives. About the Role This is a hands-on role focused on strengthening Groundwork’s political visibility, building relationships with key stakeholders, and supporting the federation to make a clear and compelling case for place-based environmental and social action. Working with the Head of Policy & Communications, the postholder will map and engage national, regional and devolved political stakeholders; maintain intelligence on policy developments and opportunities; and help Groundwork Trusts prepare for and follow up political engagement. The role will also support the development of briefings, correspondence, stakeholder materials and core messages that explain Groundwork’s role and impact. About You We are looking for someone with a genuine enthusiasm for politics, strong written communication skills and the judgement to understand what matters, what will land and how relationships are built over time. You will be organised, self-motivated and comfortable working with senior colleagues and external stakeholders across government, combined authorities, civil society and the wider policy landscape. To Apply If you would like to find out more, please click the Apply button below. You will be directed to our website where you will be able to download the Job Description and Recruitment Pack, and to complete your application for this position. When applying please clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Interview Details: Week commencing 16 November - Birmingham office. We value diversity and flexibility in our workforce as we think it gives us access to a wider range of skills. We therefore strive to be an equal opportunities employer. Where appropriate, we ask our workers to complete a Disclosure and Barring Service (Criminal Records Bureau) check. No agencies please. Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Friday 30th October 2026

item.title: Campaigns Lead
item.description: The justice system is a public service, as vital to our communities as education and healthcare. But years of underinvestment by the government have left many of us facing an uphill struggle to access legal advice when we need it. We are stepping up our efforts to secure funding for legal aid for families, and reforms to the justice system that could level the playing field for millions of people and families in England and Wales. As Campaign Lead, you will be at the heart of this work, driving forward our Legal Aid Means campaign and be at the forefront of developing new policy ideas for a justice system that serves us all, as part of a new influencing and thought leadership campaign building on the successful 21st Century Justice project. You’ll set the strategic direction, build and grow coalitions of supportive organisations, and turn new bold ideas into campaigns that get decision-makers to listen and act. You’ll bring political nous, collaborative leadership, sharp campaign management skills and an ability to engage people at every level. This role is a 12 months maternity cover. What we're looking for A proven track record of leading national-level campaigns and delivering demonstrable policy impact; Strong project and programme management skills, with the ability to prioritise and manage complex, multi-strand work; Experience leading and inspiring multi-disciplinary teams through matrix management; Confidence building relationships with a wide range of stakeholders, from senior leaders to external partners. What's in it for you This is an excellent opportunity to work with contemporary thinkers in a progressive membership organisation. The successful candidate will join a strong brand with a reputation for excellence and legal expertise, committed to promoting equality, diversity and inclusion, and a culture of trust, clarity, excellence and respect. We offer hybrid working (minimum two days a week working on site), a generous flexible benefits package, a friendly working environment and the opportunity to develop your career within a professional organisation. To Apply Please click on the Apply button below for more information and to download the Job Spec, and when applying clearly state that you saw the role through the PubAffairs network. Interviews are likely to take place on 26 and 29 October. Please note: if you are an internal applicant, Pay Policy will apply. The Law Society represents solicitors in England and Wales. From negotiating with and lobbying the profession's regulators, government and other decision makers, to offering training and advice, we're here to help, protect and promote solicitors. If you would like to have an informal discussion about the role, please contact Sorana Vieru on sorana.vieru@lawsociety.org.uk Apply Closing date The closing date for applications for this post is 11:59pm on Monday 19th October 2026
